newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Allstate would favor property deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Allstate would favor property deal.

text.p: Allstate Corp Chairman Jerry Choate said he was open to making insurance acquisitions, but said he believes the life insurance sector is overpriced and therefore would lean more toward a property-liability deal.
Although he did not rule out a life insurance deal, he said any acquisition must fit in with the company's core business and should contribute to earnings quickly.
"We would probably be more interested in property-liability," Choate said in an interview with Reuters after the company released its first quarter earnings.
"That does not mean we would not be interested in life, but the fact is the returns in the life business haven't been as good and the prices have been higher," he said.
The life insurance industry has been going through intense consolidation, with a handful of acquirors buying properties to expand their businesses and boost earnings through cost savings.
But Choate said Allstate does not need to make a life insurance acquisition and said the merger activity has driven prices too high.
"We think it's overpriced. We're not interested in doing that," he said.
Any acquisition, he said, "has to fit our core skills, has to fit our core businesses, has to be priced right, we want it to be accretive shortly, we're not interested in overpaying for anything."
"We have our eyes open all the time and we won't miss anything," he said.
Meanwhile, he said, Allstate plans to aggressively expand its business outside the United States.

He said Allstate plans to expand its operations in Japan as the country deregulates the insurance business and said the company plans further expansion, primarily in the life business, elsewhere in Asia.

"We're interested in other parts of Asia as well," Choate said. "We'll continue to move forward as soon as we're comfortable we have the right connection in terms of the country and partner, if we have partner. We're pretty far down the path with some things," he said.
He declined to give any additional details about the company's plans in Asia.
Choate also said Allstate may expand its European operations outside of Germany.
Allstate recently entered the German auto insurance market with direct telemarketing.
"We want to wait and see how this one goes and what we learn from this one and we know exactly where we'll go next there," he said.
Allstate earlier reported operating earnings of $1.26 a share, well above analysts' First Call consensus estimate of $1.17 a share.
Earnings were helped by mild weather and reduced claim volume, Choate said. In addition, he said, the recent redesign of the company's claim operation also has contributed to the favorable results.
Personal lines written premium grew 6.2 percent as a result of increased standard and non-standard auto premiums.
Choate said the non-standard auto business posted premium growth of 24 percent and said "it's a business we can still consider a rapid growth business for us."
In the life and annuity business, however, statutory premiums fell 15.1 percent in the quarter and operating income fell 3.2 percent.
Choate said group pension product sales declined as the company pulled back from that market because of the prospect for unattractive returns.
"We won't write that business unless we have the appropriate assets," he said, to match the liabilities the company accepts when it takes on the pension business.
